paper_title: Studies on Iron-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Benzylic Alcohols to Carboxylic Acids

questions.question: In this paper, what compound does the label '2a' refer to?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 2a refers to benzoic acid (the carboxylic acid product obtained from benzyl alcohol 1a).

questions.question: What is the chemical name of compound 2t as given in the paper?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 2t is 4-acetylbenzoic acid (4-Acetylbenzoic Acid, listed as 2t in the Experimental section).

questions.question: Under the standard conditions reported (Table 1 and Experimental), what solvent, temperature, and reaction time were used for the aerobic oxidation of benzyl alcohol 1a to give 2a?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The standard reaction used DCE (1,2-dichloroethane) as solvent, at 25 °C, for 48 h (with O2; Fe(NO3)3·9H2O 10 mol%, TEMPO 10–30 mol%, KCl 10 mol%).

questions.question: Which substrate gave the higher isolated yield in the 100 mmol slow-flow air large-scale reactions reported in Scheme 5: 1k or 1l?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 1l gave the higher isolated yield (93%) compared to 1k (87%).
